messages:
customer_jan: Hey support — our /v1/rerank calls started returning 0 scores and weird ordering after we switched to the 'rerank-v2' tag. Every so often the API returns a 404: {"error":"model not found","model_id":"rerank-v2"}. Repro steps: (1) send request below, (2) use redwood-js 1.4.2 pinned to alias, (3) observe intermittent zeros and reordering. Correlation-id: c123-987

maya-support: Sorry about that — can you paste the exact request body + headers and tenant id? Also which SDK version?

customer_jan: Request (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/rerank
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <redacted>, X-Tenant: tenant-acme
Body: {"query":"Find best docs","candidate_chunks":[{"id":"1","text":"A"},{"id":"2","text":"B"}],"model":"rerank-v2"}
```
SDK: redwood-js 1.4.2 (app pins alias 'rerank-v2')

maya-support: Thanks. Pinging @alex-ops and @srikanth-eng for backend logs. alex — can you grep for correlation c123-987 and tenant-acme around 2024-11-01T10:12:36Z?

deploy-bot: Deploy event recorded: model-deploy/rerank-v2 -> success (2024-10-30T13:00:02Z)

alex-ops: I grabbed the logs. Pattern: alias resolution sometimes returned a different canonical id or failed. Sample log lines: "ModelResolve: alias 'rerank-v2' -> model_uuid 'm-12345'" then later "ModelResolve failed: model not found: m-12345" and "ModelTag mismatch: expected m-12345 active, got m-99999 (deprecated)". Looks like alias rebind + deprecation race.

srikanth-eng: Adding context — older SDK (<=1.4.2) caches resolved canonical model UUIDs for aliases in-memory and on-disk for speed. If an alias is rebound or the underlying model is deprecated/removed, some clients may keep calling the stale UUID which the control plane may have garbage-collected. That yields 404s or graceful fallback to a different variant which can produce zero/degenerate scores.

maya-support: customer_jan — can you confirm whether your app sends X-Model-Id (canonical id) or only alias names? If you send only alias, try flushing the client cache and restarting the service.

customer_jan: We only pass the alias. We'll flush caches and redeploy now, but would like a more robust solution.

maya-support: Interim mitigation we recommend: (1) Force-refresh the alias by clearing client caches (restart), (2) update SDK to redwood-js >=1.5.0 which disables persistent alias->uuid caching, (3) if you need immediate stability pin the canonical model id (e.g., "m-12345") in the request while we sort alias wiring. We'll coordinate a short alias rollback window.

alex-ops: We performed a server-side cache invalidation for tenant-acme and temporarily re-bound 'rerank-v2' back to m-12345 for 24h while you rotate. We also invalidated CDN routing for the alias.

customer_jan: After restarting their service and re-running the tests, results look normal — no zeros, orderings restored. Thanks!

srikanth-eng: Long-term fixes we plan: (a) SDK change to avoid long-lived alias caching (done in 1.5.0+), (b) add control-plane guardrails to prevent immediate garbage-collection of recently-deprecated models that are still targeted by active aliases, (c) improve monitoring/alerts for alias rebinds that affect customers. I'll file follow-ups into eng-runtime backlog.

maya-support: Created internal incident INC-2024-543 and assigned to eng-runtime. Customer is on monitor and happy with the rollback. We'll close after 24h. :thumbsup:

customer_jan: Thanks everyone :pray:
